faqs.question: What should I text my best friend on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Send one short line tied to something only the two of you share: a costume disaster, a film you always watch, a nickname. Under 20 words is enough on the day if you are celebrating together; save longer messages for a friend who is far away or one you have known for 10+ years.

faqs.question: How do I wish my best friend a happy Halloween if we live in different countries?
faqs.answer: Time it for their evening, not yours, and say what you are doing where you are so they feel included. A voice note of 30 to 60 seconds works well because it carries your voice across the distance, and a link with an unlock time can open exactly at their evening.

faqs.question: What is the time difference between London and New York on Halloween?
faqs.answer: On 31 October 2026 and 31 October 2027 it is 4 hours, not the usual 5. The UK puts its clocks back on the last Sunday of October (25 October 2026, 31 October 2027), while the US ends daylight saving time on the first Sunday of November, so 8pm in New York is midnight in London.

faqs.question: What do I send a best friend who doesn't celebrate Halloween?
faqs.answer: Leave out the ghosts and costumes and keep the warmth: a plain 'thinking of you on the 31st' works. If they celebrate Diwali, note that it falls on 29 October in 2027, two days before Halloween, so one message can cover both.

faqs.question: What should I say to a best friend who is having a hard time around Halloween?
faqs.answer: Offer company or quiet without asking them to be cheerful or to explain. Research on best-friend support found that very heavy co-rumination, going over the problem again and again, can add stress, so presence matters more than a long debrief. A phone call is often better than any text.

faqs.question: Is it okay to roast my best friend in a Halloween message?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the joke is about something they already laugh at, like a recycled costume or jumping at every balloon. Avoid looks, weight and anything they are sensitive about, and never roast a friend who is going through a rough patch.

faqs.question: How long should a Halloween message for a best friend be?
faqs.answer: Under 20 words for a same-day text, one or two sentences for a supportive private message, and 40 to 80 words for a card to a long-time friend. In a group chat, one line with a single question or vote gets the most replies.

faqs.question: Can I use the SubhSandesh Halloween page for my whole friend group?
faqs.answer: No, it is a one-person greeting page, not a party or group tool. For the bestie group chat, use plain group lines; make the page for the one friend you want to surprise.

faqs.question: What is bestie mode on the SubhSandesh Halloween page?
faqs.answer: It changes the closing question and licence for a best friend: by default the question becomes 'Will you be my boo-st friend forever?'. The friend still knocks three times, carves a pumpkin until your word glows, finds up to six of your photos and reads your letter by flashlight, and you get an email the first time they answer.

faqs.question: When should I send a Halloween message to my best friend?
faqs.answer: On 31 October itself, in their evening if they live elsewhere. A quick text on the day beats a polished message that arrives on 1 November.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Messages for Best Friend: 57 Lines for Every Situation

Good Halloween messages for a best friend fit where the friendship is right now: beside you in costume, in another time zone, in a hard month, or new enough that a text still feels risky. Below are 57 original, clean lines in nine situations, with blanks for your own inside jokes.

If you send a link, write for a phone: across SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on one, and each page averages 11.1 views. Those are platform-wide figures, not Halloween data. You also get time-zone maths for 31 October and a format table.

## What makes a Halloween message for a best friend work?

A Halloween message for a best friend is a short text, card line or voice note for 31 October that says something only you two would get. The costume is the excuse; the shared history is the message.

In [Roberts and Dunbar's 18-month study of 25 students](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4626528) (Human Nature, 2015), closeness to family rose after leaving school while closeness to friends fell. Effort slowed the slide: talking for women, shared activities for men. A Halloween message is an excuse for both.

## 57 Halloween messages for your best friend, by situation

Each group matches one situation. Swap the brackets for your own names and disasters.

### 1. You're celebrating together

Send these on the day. Keep them under 20 words.

- "Costume check at 7? Bring the glue gun and your worst ideas."
- "Splitting my emergency chocolate stash with you tonight. Nobody else qualifies."
- "Our door, our sweets bowl, our terrible playlist. See you at six, partner in crime."
- "Tonight's rule: whoever screams first in the haunted maze buys chips after."
- "Reminder: last year you jumped at a fake spider. I've packed tissues and a camera."
- "Of all the haunted houses on our street, my favourite is still the one you live in."

### 2. You're apart this year

These assume different clocks. Check the time-zone section below first.

- "Same tradition, new time zone: I'm narrating our film to your empty chair tonight."
- "Happy Halloween from [city]. Nobody here does the voices like you do."
- "It's [time] here and [time] there. Send me your costume before bed or I'm choosing it for you."
- "First Halloween in years without you at my door. The sweets bowl is suspiciously full."
- "Voice note incoming: me attempting your witch laugh. Please rate it out of ten."
- "Miles apart, but I carved your initials into a pumpkin. It looks slightly worried."

### 3. Inside-joke templates with fill-in blanks

Fill each bracket with something only your friend knows. Memory beats puns.

- "Happy Halloween to my [nickname]. Still not over the [event] of [year]."
- "This year's costume: [the thing you said at that party]. You know exactly why."
- "If [name] knocks tonight, we're pretending we're not home. Again."
- "Spotted a [object] today and laughed out loud alone in a shop. Your fault."
- "Tonight's soundtrack is [song you ruined forever]. You're welcome."
- "Brewing a potion tonight: one part [your catchphrase], two parts [our snack], a pinch of [that trip]."

### 4. Your friend is going through a rough patch

Drop the jokes and offer company, not a debrief. A [2025 study of 187 Dutch adolescents](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12217408) (Journal of Adolescence) linked best-friend support to lower depression and stress, but very high co-rumination, going over a problem again and again, turned support into more stress.

- "No costume needed. I'm around tonight, for company or for quiet."
- "Skipping Halloween is allowed. I'll bring soup and sweets either way, your call."
- "Not asking you to be cheerful. Just reminding you I'm in your corner, ghosts and all."
- "If tonight feels like too much, text me one emoji and I'll take it from there."
- "Happy Halloween, gently. You don't owe anyone a smile this week, including me."
- "Putting a film on at eight. There's a blanket on the sofa with your name on it."

### 5. Your friend doesn't celebrate Halloween

Some friends skip it for faith or taste, so keep the spooky out. For Indian friends, [Diwali falls on 29 October 2027](https://www.drikpanchang.com/diwali/diwali-puja-calendar.html?year=2027), two days before Halloween; in 2026 it is 8 November.

- "No pumpkins required. Just thinking of you on the 31st, the way I do most days."
- "Not a Halloween person? Fine. Here's a completely non-spooky hello."
- "When Diwali and Halloween land in the same week, I'm celebrating you twice."
- "Skipping the scary part and keeping the sweet part, which is you."
- "Happy end of October! No costumes, just gratitude for you."
- "You enjoy your quiet night in, I'll handle the doorbell. Breakfast on the 1st?"

### 6. Long-time friends (10+ years)

After a decade, lean on history, not wit. A real number of years lands.

- "Fifteen Halloweens and counting. Our costumes got worse; we got better."
- "You've seen me as a bin-bag ghost and still kept my number. That's loyalty."
- "Ten years ago we argued over the witch hat. Today it's yours."
- "We've outlived three flatmates, a lot of fake blood and two of your phones. Here's to more."
- "Same porch steps we sat on at twelve, older knees. Happy Halloween to you."
- "Still the first person I'd call if a house was actually haunted."

### 7. A newer friend you want to get closer to

A light invitation beats a declaration. Give them an easy yes.

- "Our first Halloween as friends, so the bar is low: sweets and a bad film?"
- "Still not sure if you're a scary-film person or a cosy-film person. Tonight would settle it."
- "Happy Halloween! Glad our [class/office/gym] put us in the same corner."
- "I'm carving a pumpkin this weekend and could use a second pair of hands. Free?"
- "Fair warning: I am a lot on 31 October. Hope you're ready."
- "Happy Halloween to my newest favourite person. Next year, matching costumes."
- "Thanks for making this city feel less spooky. Happy Halloween."

### 8. Funny roast-style (kind)

Roast only what your friend already laughs at. Skip looks and sore spots.

- "You've worn the same cat ears for six years. Bold. Iconic. Please wash them."
- "Your pumpkin carving peaked at age nine and I respect that."
- "Can't wait to watch you jump when a balloon pops. Happy Halloween, brave one."
- "You're the only ghost I know who still owes me a fiver."
- "Reminder that last year's costume was a hoodie and a confident attitude."
- "Happy Halloween to my favourite spoiler-checker, who reads every horror plot before pressing play."
- "You're going as a vampire? Finally, an excuse for those 2am replies."

### 9. Group-chat lines for the bestie group

Group messages need a job: a vote, a deadline or a photo request. One question per line stops the scroll.

- "Roll call: costumes, meeting point, snacks. Answer by Thursday or you're wearing the ghost sheet."
- "Bestie group, it's 31 October. Photos in here by midnight or it didn't happen."
- "Vote: scary film, cosy film or both back to back? Thumbs up for chaos."
- "Happy Halloween to this group chat, the scariest thing on my phone."
- "Pinning this: costume theme is 'things we've lost in [friend]'s car'."
- "Our group photo from last Halloween is still my lock screen. Let's beat it."
- "Half of us are far away, so everyone post one pumpkin photo. I'll make the collage."

## What time should you send it across countries?

Send for their evening, not yours, and check the clocks: 31 October falls in changeover week. The UK [puts its clocks back on 25 October 2026 and 31 October 2027](https://www.gov.uk/when-do-the-clocks-change); the US [ends daylight saving time](https://www.nist.gov/pml/time-and-frequency-division/popular-links/daylight-saving-time-dst) on the first Sunday of November (1 November 2026).

So on Halloween 2026 and 2027, London is 4 hours ahead of New York, not 5: 8pm trick-or-treating in New York is midnight in London. India keeps one clock, so an 8pm text from Mumbai lands at 2.30pm in London and 10.30am in New York.

## Which message format fits which situation?

Five situations, matched to a channel and a length. Lengths are editorial guidance, not measured data; 60 seconds is the premium page's voice-note limit.

| Situation | Best format | Length | Example from this list |
|---|---|---|---|
| Celebrating together | Text on the day | Under 20 words | "Costume check at 7?..." |
| Apart, different countries | Voice note timed to their evening | 30–60 seconds | "Voice note incoming..." |
| Rough patch | Private text, never the group | 1–2 sentences | "No costume needed..." |
| Long-time friend (10+ years) | Card or one-person page | 40–80 words | "Fifteen Halloweens and counting..." |
| Bestie group | Group message with one question | 1 line plus a vote | "Vote: scary film, cosy film..." |

The further apart or older the friendship, the longer the format can be. Same-room friends need one line.

## When to turn the message into a Halloween page

For a decade-long friend, one text can feel small. The [Halloween card in bestie mode](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is something they play: three knocks on a haunted house, a pumpkin carved until your word glows, up to six of your photos behind foggy portraits, and your letter by flashlight. Its final question becomes "Will you be my boo-st friend forever?", and you are emailed when they first answer.

For the friend abroad, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds a 60-second voice note, up to 12 photos and an optional unlock time, so it opens at their evening. On SubhSandesh, 38.5% of creators password-protect a page before sharing, which suits jokes nobody else should read. For other occasions, browse the [template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

## When a Halloween message is the wrong move

Both pages greet one person, not a party, so the group chat needs plain text. The interface is English only.

Timing beats polish. In SubhSandesh's Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself: another festival, only 89 pages, but most people send on the day. A friend who is struggling needs a phone call more than any line above.

## Sources

- Roberts and Dunbar (2015). [Managing Relationship Decay: Network, Gender, and Contextual Effects](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4626528). Human Nature, 21 October 2015.
- van der Mey-Baijens et al. (2025). [Co-Rumination as a Moderator Between Best-Friend Support and Adolescent Psychological Distress](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12217408). Journal of Adolescence, 16 February 2025.
- GOV.UK. [When do the clocks change?](https://www.gov.uk/when-do-the-clocks-change) Updated 24 November 2025.
- NIST. [Daylight Saving Time Rules](https://www.nist.gov/pml/time-and-frequency-division/popular-links/daylight-saving-time-dst).
- Drik Panchang. [2027 Diwali Puja Calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/diwali/diwali-puja-calendar.html?year=2027).
